📚 Today you learned

Bolt-on Acquisition vs. Transformational M&A

SPXC's $410M all-cash FIS Water deal is a bolt-on: it adds a related product line (water management/control for industrial cooling) inside a segment SPX already operates in, funded from the balance sheet, contributing ~$105M revenue against a company already doing well over $2B. Compare that to a transformational deal — buying into a new segment entirely, usually funded with debt or heavy stock dilution, that changes what the company actually is. Bolt-ons are lower-risk: the integration playbook is known, and a bad one rarely sinks the stock. Transformational deals are binary bets on strategy — they can re-rate a company overnight, for better or worse. When you see a company you hold announce M&A, the first question is which type it is; SPXC's is the boring, low-risk kind, and it's irrelevant to why you're exiting the position (that's the separate Kranze defense-segment issue).

Also today: Accretive vs. dilutive — whether a deal adds to or subtracts from per-share earnings in the near term; an all-cash bolt-on like FIS Water is typically accretive almost immediately since there's no new share count to dilute against.
